subject: general
question: Asexual reproduction by fragmentation occurs:

options.text: only in simple body organised multicellular organisms
only in complex body organised multicellular organisms

solution:
The correct answer is __**only in simple body organised multicellular organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fragmentation** is a type of asexual reproduction where an organism breaks into fragments, each capable of growing independently into a new organism.
 
• It primarily occurs in **simple body organized multicellular organisms** such as algae, fungi, and some plants like liverworts.
 
• This method of reproduction ensures rapid population growth and survival in stable environments.
 
• Examples include **species like Spirogyra** (a type of green algae) and certain fungi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• It involves a single parent and produces offspring genetically identical to the parent.
 
• Types include binary fission, budding, spore formation, and fragmentation.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**
 
 
• Common in unicellular organisms like bacteria and protozoa.
 
• The organism splits into two equal halves, each becoming a new individual.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• Occurs in organisms like yeast and hydra.
 
• A new organism grows from a bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation**
 
 
• Seen in fungi, algae, and some plants.
 
• Reproduction occurs through the release of spores, which are resistant to adverse conditions.
